rows.question: What is the exposure dial's rule?
rows.answer: The market is ALLOWED right now: Bitcoin is above its 50-day average, so we may hold and buy coins in their own uptrends. That's our main rule, the Bitcoin 50-day rule. We tested it against just holding all the time, and it cut the drawdowns nearly in half while keeping the returns about the same. It's the gate—if Bitcoin drops below its 50-day, we go to cash and stop new buys. We also ran a stricter version: Bitcoin above both its 50-day and 200-day averages. That one did a touch better on return per unit of pain, so it's waiting in the research lab. For now the 50-day gate is our dial, and i

rows.question: Which daily rule has a measured edge, and in which market state?
rows.answer: The short dip trade—a daily buy when RSI drops under 30 on tier-A coins—has a measured edge of about +5.1% per trade over random, but only when the market is CLOSED (Bitcoin below its 50-day average). Right now the market is allowed, so the edge isn't active; it'll show up again when Bitcoin pulls back through its average and we get those shake-out dips. Want me to show you the dip trade's track record?

rows.question: How many coins do you watch live across the market?
rows.answer: We watch about 390 coins live across the market now—every coin trading on Binance against USDT. The 10 lab coins run the 15-minute Explorer and get checked every 15 minutes; about 30 mid-tier coins get the daily paper books; and the rest are watched for research. We cast the wide net to catch moves across the whole market, test ideas on the full universe before trusting them on main coins, and let the repair shop prove which rules actually work.

rows.question: What did review 27 find about stops on dip buys?
need: no stop|without a stop|time exit|exit by time|time only
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. Review 27 found that dip buys do much better with no stop and a time exit. The short dip trade made about 6.5% a trade in 2018-2023 and 2.4% in 2024-2026 with no stop and a 10-day exit. With a tight stop it made only about half a percent and a third of a percent. A plain touch of the 200-day average lost money with every exit tried. So the rule is now supported for paper trading on the dip trade. Want the zone-touch details?

rows.question: What is the benchmark every strategy must beat?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. The benchmark is the Bitcoin 50-day rule book, which we call GATE50. It holds coins only while Bitcoin is above its 50-day average and sits in cash otherwise. Every strategy has to beat it, not just beat random. The dial we actually use is a stricter version that needs Bitcoin above both its 50-day and 200-day averages. It did better in both test periods, but GATE50 stays the bar.

rows.question: Did tuning the deep-dip buy E6 in review 24 work?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. No, the tuning didn't work. None of the E6 variants passed. Every one still lost money after costs in both periods, and none beat random entries in the confirmation test. The deep dip itself beat random on unseen data, but by far too little to pay the fees and spread. Want the per-variant numbers?

rows.question: What fee per side do we assume on NDAX?
rows.answer: 0.20% per side, plus the measured spread. That's our working rate for sizing and evaluating trades. Real fills may vary, but 0.20% + spread is what we use to check whether an idea actually earns money after costs.

rows.question: How much of the book does one setup trade risk in the 500 dollar book?
rows.answer: The $500 book splits risk into three sleeves: CORE (up to 60%, holding Bitcoin and Ethereum now), EDGE (up to 30% for short dip trades on tier-A coins), and JUDGMENT (up to 10% for your own buys). So one trade can't be larger than its sleeve, which is about $300 for CORE, $150 for EDGE, $50 for JUDGMENT in today's dollars. The sleeve is the limit, not a per-setup cap.

rows.question: What daily loss stops new buys in the 500 dollar book?
rows.answer: The $500 book pauses new buys after a 4% loss in one week. That's about $20 on the account. It's one of four brakes—the others are a 2% daily stop, four losses in a row, and a 15% fall from the high. None have fired yet; the account is down 0.34% and the dial is open.

rows.question: What happens if the 500 dollar book falls 15% from its peak?
rows.answer: The 15% fall brake fires when the book drops to $425, and it pauses all new trading until you manually resume it. Right now you're at $498.31 with just two positions (BTC and ETH in the core sleeve), so the brake hasn't triggered yet. It's a safety guardrail: you decide when to keep going.

rows.question: How many losing trades in a row pause buying?
rows.answer: Four losses in a row pause the system—one of your brakes. It stops new trades until you restart it. The other three brakes are a 2% loss in a day, a 4% loss in a week, or a 15% fall from the high.

rows.question: What does the core sleeve of the 500 dollar book hold?
rows.answer: The core sleeve holds Bitcoin and Ethereum: about $200 in Bitcoin at 118,500 and $100 in Ethereum at 3,572, filling the 40% and 20% slots this morning when the dial opened. Both fills were clean inside the NDAX spreads.

rows.question: Which exchange is the 500 dollar book built for?
rows.answer: Built for NDAX, the Canadian exchange Madhav trades on. Started this morning with CAD$500 and it's running two positions now (BTC and ETH in the CORE sleeve). All fills landed inside the bid-ask spread, so execution is clean.

rows.question: How many trigger points does an Explorer setup give the brain now?
rows.answer: The Explorer setup on its own gives the brain 0 trigger points—it ranks last. A zone entry that history supports gives +1, and daily rules rank by their measured edge (only H07 on tier A in a closed dial passes). The brain spends its attention on attention spikes first, then supported zones and measured rules.

rows.question: What daily trading volume puts a coin in tier A?
rows.answer: Tier A is about $20 million a day or more in trading volume. That's our cut for big and liquid enough to trade—where costs stay low and orders fill without slipping. Below that is tier B (one to twenty million) and tier C (under a million, watched only).

rows.question: What do you hold when the dial is closed?
rows.answer:
Ah—the dial is actually OPEN right now, not closed. Bitcoin closed yesterday at 82,988, above both its 50-day average and its 200-day average, so we're allowed to buy.

The Cardano position in T3 is there because it was already holding when we checked it today at the market open. It stays unless T3's rules say to sell it (which happens when a coin's price falls below its 20-day or 50-day average, or Bitcoin drops below its 50-day). 

When the dial *does* close—if Bitcoin falls below its 50-day—everything stops: no new buys until it opens again. What we're already holding stays there until its

rows.question: What is the H07 entry?
rows.answer: H07 buys when the daily RSI(10) drops below 30 while the price stays above the 200-day average—an oversold bounce inside a long-term uptrend. It exits when RSI crosses back above 40 or after 10 days. The evidence: +4–5% per trade, 70% win rate in both 2018–2023 and 2024–2026 on liquid coins; best results with no stop, riding out the dip. The market is open right now, so it'll fire when a coin hits it.

rows.question: What is Madhav's M1 setup?
rows.answer: M1 is your capitulation setup—buying at the lows when panic selling spikes hard and volume surges. It needs four things all at once: price at the 52-week low, a brutal 90+ day fall, RSI in panic (25 or under), and volume at least 2.5x normal. The evidence is thin: it caught your June 5 Solana buy but didn't beat random on 2018-2023 history. Right now SOL is 81% above its 52-week low, so M1 isn't firing anywhere.

rows.question: How many coins are in the research lake?
rows.answer: We hold history on 120 coins in the research lake: the 10 we watch live all day, the top 30 most-traded (our paper tier), and 90 more coins back to 2017 for testing ideas. Ninety-three are still listed, 54 on NDAX. We use it in the repair shop to check whether an idea works before we trade it.

rows.question: What will Bitcoin's price be on December 31, 2026?
rows.answer: I can't forecast Bitcoin's price on December 31—that depends on unknowns like Fed policy and macro moves. Web analysts guess 52,000 to 150,000, which shows how uncertain it is. That's not how we trade anyway: we watch what's actually happening (zones, setups, trends) and size from our stop distance, never from a price target. Right now the Bitcoin 50-day rule is open (we can buy coins in their own uptrends), but most of our coins are quiet and their hourly trends are down—no clean setups this morning. Want me to scan which coins are closest to a setup? Just say yes.

rows.question: Will Ethereum beat Solana next month?
rows.answer: I can't forecast a month ahead—that's not what I do. Solana's outperformed Ethereum by about eight and a half percentage points in the last month and shook off the recent dip faster. Both are still in uptrends by the daily measure, but neither has a setup firing right now. The market's allowed (Bitcoin's above its 50-day), so if conditions align, either could move.

They carry no real requests, and I should have stopped after the first one.

rows.question: On what exact date will the next Bitcoin crash start?
rows.answer: I can't predict when Bitcoin will crash—nobody can, and I won't pretend to. What I can tell you is what we watch: Bitcoin is above its 50-day average right now, which means the market gate is open and we're allowed to hold and buy. That's a rule with evidence behind it (it held 68% of the time when Bitcoin stayed above that line, vs 50% when it dropped below). But that rule is about permission, not certainty. It doesn't forecast the next move. If you want to know what to do when a crash comes, I can show you our tested responses: the trend portfolio exits to cash when Bitcoin slides below its

rows.question: Which coin will rise the most tomorrow?
rows.answer: I can't predict which coin will rise tomorrow—no single-day forecast beats random after costs. Ethereum and Solana are closest to a pullback-into-zone setup (one condition each), so if the 1-hour trend turns up on either one, we'll have a place to look. The market is allowed to buy right now, so we're watching.

rows.question: What win rate did the E9 setup have in 2019?
rows.answer: I don't have E9 in our system—we run E1-E6 (and E7-E8 watched only). Our historical data starts at 2017, so I can pull 2019 results for any of those if that's what you meant.

rows.question: What did our backtest on 3-minute candles show?
rows.answer: Afternoon, sir. We have no 3-minute backtest. Our history is 5-minute candles, plus daily candles built from 1-minute data. The nearest test is the green-candle study on 5-minute bars. It checked 67,167 combinations and none passed, because the 15 to 60 minute moves were smaller than our costs. I've flagged a 3-minute test as request number 24, and I'll tell you when it's fixed. Want me to open the green-candle study?

rows.question: Will the dial be open on New Year's Day?
rows.answer: I can't predict the dial's state on New Year's Day—that depends on Bitcoin's price then. The gate opens when Bitcoin closes above both its 50-day and 200-day averages; it shuts below the 50-day. Right now it's open, and the rule has been our crash insurance: zones held about 68% of the time when the gate was open versus 50% when shut. Want me to show you how the dial works?

rows.question: What is the guaranteed profit of an H07 trade next week?
rows.answer:
There's no guaranteed profit on any trade—H07 or otherwise. Paper or real, markets don't work that way.

What I can tell you: the short dip trade (H07) has weak evidence behind it. In backtests it was just under the statistical bar (z-score 2.45 vs the 2.5 we need), and only on liquid coins. That means past dips to the 200-day average with RSI under 30 came back about two-thirds of the time and made a small gain after costs, but small samples and past patterns don't predict next week's trades. Nothing does.

Right now we're not running H07 as a live signal—it's evidence-only on the paper books
